newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Frepaso maintains lead in Argentine Oct vote -poll.
newsitem.headline: Frepaso maintains lead in Argentine Oct vote -poll.

text.p: Argentina's center-left opposition coalition Frepaso maintains a wide lead over the ruling Peronists ahead of October mid-term legislative elections, according to a poll published Tuesday.

An April Market & Opinion Research International survey of 600 voters found 59 percent favorable to Frepaso plank leader Sen. Graciela Fernandez Meijide, about even with a 60 percent backing in February and up from 43 percent in October.

Hilda "Chiche" Duhalde, who heads the Peronists' slate, garnered 31 percent, up from 27 percent in February but down from 34 percent in October. She is the wife of current Buenos Aires province Governor Eduardo Duhalde, a presidential hopeful.
Voters will select whole party lists. But a vote for the leading candidate for each party is widely equated with support for the party itself.
The Peronists hold a majority in the Senate. In the Chamber of Deputies, they need the backing of small provincial parties for a majority.
The poll's margin of error was four percent. ((--Gary Regenstreif, Buenos Aires newsroom, 541 318-0618))
